predecessors.name: Far Eastern Republic
predecessors.text: Vladivostok and the Maritime Province, which the 1921 coup took out of the Far Eastern Republic

successors.name: Far Eastern Republic
successors.text: 'the Soviet army of the Far Eastern Republic retook most of the Priamurye Government territory' as the Japanese withdrew (June to October 1922); Vladivostok on 25 October 1922

successors.name: Soviet Union
successors.text: the Ayano-Maysky District around Ayan on the Sea of Okhotsk, 'controlled by Anatoly Pepelyayev'

rulers.name: Spiridon Merkulov
rulers.title: head of the Provisional Government (with his brother Nikolai)

rulers.name: Mikhail Diterikhs
rulers.title: voyevoda of the Priamursky Zemsky Krai

ledger.x: 1921, 27 May: a White coup in Vladivostok sets up the Provisional Priamurye Government, 'the last Russian State enclave during the Russian Civil War'.
1922, 25 October: the Far Eastern Republic retakes Vladivostok and most of the enclave.
1923, 16 June: the last White enclave surrenders.

wars.name: Far Eastern campaign of the Russian Civil War (Priamurye)
wars.outcome: The Far Eastern Republic's army retook Vladivostok on 25 October 1922 after the Japanese withdrawal and Soviet Russia absorbed the republic on 15 November 1922; Pepelyayev surrendered the Ayano-Maysky District in June 1923, 'the end of the Russian Civil War'.

wars.name: Siberian Intervention (Japanese withdrawal from the Priamurye)
wars.outcome: Japanese troops screened the enclave as 'a cordon sanitaire' and left between June and October 1922; the Far Eastern Republic page: they 'announced on 24 June 1922 that it would remove all of its troops from Siberia by the end of October'.

certainty.note: An enclave held behind a Japanese cordon, then a coastal pocket; the pages give no boundary line, so all edges are approximate.
